body.x: Panasonic announced that it has a new brand slogan: “ideas for life.” The slogan means that they are planning on communicating directly with customers and business partners across the globe. And as part of their effort to improve communication, they will be displaying a variety of new products including cameras and well-being electronic goods at KES 2012.

The product that is likely to catch the most eyes is the Lumix DMC-LX7 high-end digital camera. This comes equipped with the 24-90mm F1.4 (35mm conversion, 3.8x optics) Leica DC Vario-Summilux, the brightest lens available for compact cameras today. This camera allows photographers to get that “blurry background” effect.
The camera can also record video in full HD resolution (1,920x1,080). Users can manually adjust the exposure during recording and can also activate a feature that compensates for shaky hands.

The camera supports a maximum ISO setting of 12,000, while shutter speeds of 1/4000 of a second are possible. It features a 1/1.7 inch/12.7 megapixel MOS image sensor, and the image processing engine is Panasonic’s Venus engine. It comes with a 3 inch/.92-megapixel LCD and it supports the Auto Power LCD that automatically adjusts between 11 levels of screen brightness according to the lighting around you. There are 40MB of internal memory, and the device uses SD and SDHC memory cards. With one charge of the battery, you can take around 330 pictures.

While the Lumix DMC-LX7 is a product for ordinary consumers, the AG-HPX600P that is displayed alongside it is designed for pros. This device is an ENG broadcasting camcorder that supports the AVC-U codec. The camera has a MOS sensor that is 2/3 inches in size and features Wi-Fi capability so that you can review videos you have captured on a tablet computer.
